name: Residences on Acoma
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Second Chance Center, a Denver reentry nonprofit, is building Residences on Acoma at 1501 S. Acoma Street: 128 apartments, 60 of them supportive homes at 30% AMI for people who have been homeless or in the justice system and 68 workforce homes at 60% AMI, financed partly by a 2022 Round Two award of 4% and state housing tax credits.
why_it_matters: A reentry nonprofit is acting as sole general partner, guarantor and owner, with BlueLine as fee developer. The deal pairs Division of Housing vouchers with apprenticeship-linked workforce units and stacks Denver homelessness-fund money, a federal earmark and Enterprise equity and CDFI loans. It is a template for justice-involved supportive housing.

status.label: Under construction since May 2024; opening not confirmed
status.detail: Groundbreaking was held on 2024-05-06. An undated Colorado Gives fundraising page said the building was 40% complete and due to finish by November 2025. No public certificate of occupancy, opening or lease-up record was found as of 2026-10-21.

next_step: Watch for a Denver certificate of occupancy for 1501 S. Acoma Street and a Second Chance Center opening announcement.

key_numbers.meaning: 121 one-bedrooms and 7 two-bedrooms. The 60 supportive units (57 one-bedroom, 3 two-bedroom) have Division of Housing project-based vouchers.

key_numbers.value: $1,619,731 a year in federal 4% credit plus $953,024 of state credit
key_numbers.meaning: About $16.2M in federal credit over 10 years (inferred). The application asked for $1,596,929 federal and $1,000,000 state.
Approved unanimously on the council's consent agenda in March 2024, from the homelessness resolution fund and the affordable housing fund.

key_numbers.value: $16M federal and $4M state credit equity from Enterprise
key_numbers.meaning: Enterprise's CDFI also lent $2.5M for site acquisition and $1M for predevelopment.

facts.value: Residences on Acoma, LLLP. Second Chance Center is sole general partner, guarantor and owner.
Four-story wood-frame building over 60 underground parking spaces, two elevators, about 10,860 sq ft of first-floor office and service space, a courtyard, and NGBS certification targeted
Zoned I-MX-5. The site is level and vacant, and a prior owner had soil abatement done. It is near three light rail stations, and the market study flagged light rail noise.

WellPower (formerly Mental Health Center of Denver) is lead provider for the supportive units. Second Chance Center offers career services and paid apprenticeships to all residents. Funding comes from Medicaid, Division of Housing Tenant Support Services, Denver supportive services grants, WAGEES funding, the 5% developer fee boost and cash flow.

money.note: The application asked for $1,000,000. Its narrative treats that as $6,000,000 over six years, so the figure appears to be an annual amount (inferred).
Plus a planned $6,139,000 taxable bond, for $29,621,000 of construction financing. $17,300,000 permanent tax-exempt debt was expected.

money.source: City and County of Denver loan
money.note: From the voter-approved homelessness resolution fund and the affordable housing fund (Department of Housing Stability)

background.text: Land deal: Second Chance Center bought the site in January 2022 and planned to sell it to the partnership at closing. Enterprise's CDFI provided a $2.5M acquisition loan.

This is Second Chance Center's second deal with BlueLine, after Providence at the Heights, a 50-unit supportive building in Aurora. Second Chance Center went through an investor-set capacity program to become sole general partner.

Community outreach: an information meeting on 2021-07-22 drew 74 attendees from neighborhood groups and the district council office. A second meeting on 2022-06-28 at Platt Park Recreation Center raised no issues after the parking design changed.
Workforce units are meant for referrals from Second Chance Center's apprenticeship programs. The application reports that 2021 apprenticeship completers averaged $22.87 an hour.

Local approvals: Denver City Council approved the $5.35M loan agreement unanimously on its consent agenda at a Tuesday meeting reported on 2024-03-28. The council bill or resolution number was not found.

timeline.event: Second Chance Center buys the site
Second community meeting at Platt Park Recreation Center
CHFA announces the 2022 Round Two awards (listed as 'Residences at Acoma')
Denver City Council approves the $5.35M loan (Tuesday meeting; date inferred from the 2024-03-28 report)
Targeted construction completion (undated fundraising page); not confirmed

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award description, applicant report and news release call the project 'Residences at Acoma', while the award report, narrative and later press use 'Residences on Acoma'.

CHFA and the application describe the 68 non-supportive units as 60% AMI family or workforce housing, while Enterprise's groundbreaking story says those 68 units are dedicated to people experiencing homelessness or leaving the justice system.
The award report shows $1,619,731 federal and $953,024 state credit, while the applicant report shows $1,596,929 federal and $1,000,000 state.

open_questions: Whether construction finished and residents moved in. No certificate of occupancy, opening or lease-up record was found.
Bond closing date, final development cost, construction lender and general contractor (Calcon gave only the application estimate) are not public.
Amounts of Division of Housing grant and Denver Housing Authority support, and any property tax exemption, were not found.
Denver council resolution number, affordability covenant term, and placed-in-service and 8609 dates are not public.
No public site plan or rendering was found. The CHFA narrative pages hold only a generic header image.
